subject: Log access patterns and BYOK integration coordination
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@medflux.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-01-17T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on log access patterns + BYOK for upcoming SOC3 review

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for taking this. We’re preparing for a scoped SOC3 spot-check and have a few clarifying questions around the audit data Redwood can provide and how BYOK/KMS affects evidence delivery. High-level asks below: 

1) Log fields: we need a mapping of the audit log fields you retain (timestamp, requester identity, route/model, tokenized lengths, error codes, IP/region, KV cache hits, etc.). Is there a CSV or table you can share?
2) Access model: when a customer uses Private/BYOK, can Redwood still produce an unredacted audit export for an authorized auditor (read-only), or does key separation block any readable event data?
3) Retention options: what are the default retention windows per deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private) and what carve-outs can we request for short-term retention (30/90/180 days)?
4) SSO: will we be able to map SSO identities to audit events (SAML aud: or OIDC sub) or do events only show internal service principals?

Attached is our requirement matrix (medflux_audit_requirements.pdf) — it’s a short doc with column-level asks. Can you confirm which items you can meet out-of-the-box and which will require an exception or engineering work? We’re on a tight timeline: evidence due to our auditor by 2027-02-05.

Appreciate a quick run-down and proposed next steps. If easier, happy to schedule a 30m call this week.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Director, Security & Compliance
MedFlux Health

Subject: Re: Questions on log access patterns + BYOK for upcoming SOC3 review

Elena — thanks for the clear matrix and timeline. I’ll summarize what we can provide quickly and route the technical pieces to Marcus and Karthik. Quick answers up front:

- We have an audit field map; I’ll attach the current CSV and a short notes file for ingestion semantics.
- Private/BYOK: key separation does limit some decryptable payloads; however we can produce aggregated and most metadata fields for auditors, and for select customers we’ve delivered ironclad read-only export flows when the key owner approves — that is an exception path we can operationalize.
- Retention: hosted default is 90 days; Dedicated can be configured at contract time (30–365 days); Private depends on customer infra but we support short windows in our orchestration — details below.
- SSO mapping: we log both the SSO subject when available and a paired internal service principal for system actions. There are nuances for ephemeral sessions.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus: produce the audit-field CSV and a short technical note on fields we can always provide vs fields blocked by BYOK.
2) Karthik: outline SSO identity mapping cases and implications for auditor correlation.
3) Priya/Product: confirm if we can commit to a short 30–90 day retention carve-out and what process we need to route (legal/contract/engineering).

Can the team aim to send the attachments and a short internal memo by EOD tomorrow so I can reply to MedFlux and lock a 30m call? Elena — are mornings PST on Tuesday or Wednesday OK?

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Manager, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on log access patterns + BYOK for upcoming SOC3 review

Rachel / team — attaching the field map and ops notes. See attachments: audit-log-fieldmap-v2.csv, ingest-ops-notes.md.

Summary of technical constraints:
- Fields we can always export: event_id, event_ts (ISO8601), requester_id (SSO sub or service principal), route/model, http_status, error_code, token_count, region, client_ip (hashed if privacy mode enabled), cache_hit (bool), request_headers (redacted).
- Fields potentially blocked by BYOK: plaintext payloads, raw prompts/responses, any content encrypted client-side. If a customer has opted for client-side encryption with keys never shared, we can only provide metadata unless the customer grants a decryption token or an auditor is given temporary access.
- Retention default matrix: hosted=90d (rolling), dedicated=contract-configurable (min30d), private=customer-configured; in practice we support 7–365d ranges.
- Export mechanics: we support on-demand exports to an S3 bucket (cross-account) with a signed role; for Private deployments we can push to customer-owned storage if network policies allow.

Operational notes: for auditor work we recommend:
1) Scoped S3 export with object keys per-day and a manifest file.
2) Provide field-level schema and a sample day (sanitized) first to validate format.
3) If BYOK blocks content, we can offer either a) auditor access with customer-signed decryption token, or b) an expert witness attestation and metadata-only export.

Attaching files now.

Subject: Re: Questions on log access patterns + BYOK for upcoming SOC3 review

Couple of clarifications from product/SSO side:
- SSO mapping: when customers use enterprise SAML/SCIM, we persist the assertion subject (saml:nameid) and when present, OIDC sub for OAuth flows. For cross-session correlation we also emit a session_id correlated to the internal service principal. That combination is sufficient for auditors to tie user actions to identities in most cases.
- Ephemeral sessions/short-lived tokens: ephemeral sessions produce event records with a transient subject; we flag them as ephemeral and include a mapping entry in the export, but the auditor will need to accept that session metadata is the primary correlation method for that timeframe.
- BYOK: For Private installs where the customer manages keys in their KMS (cloud HSM), we do not hold decryption keys. Two ops paths: (1) customer provides a time-limited decryption token to us (rare), or (2) we perform a cross-account S3 export of metadata-only and the customer runs a local decrypt step, supplying a verified manifest to the auditor.

Impact to roadmap / ask: if MedFlux needs an out-of-the-box auditor access flow for BYOK customers (i.e., Redwood to temporarily unlock content for auditor after authorization), we need Product + Legal sign-off. That would be a feature request (security exception workflow) and could be scoped as a Q2 engineering deliverable if prioritized.

Related docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b-ExampleEvidence (contains sample export format and a small playbook).

-Karthik
Director, Product — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
